meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided on it, and did anyone speak to him first?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what that zero is based on.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing those down. Plenty of kids draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale, so this tells you when the essay landed in that file, not who wrote it.
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.

So now Owen has to prove himself to get back a mark you took before anyone spoke to him. Procedure 4.1 says you talk to the student first, and 4.3 says you look at his other work. Have you done either?
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
You didn't answer me, but fine. Read me the line he quoted, word for word. Seventeen-year-olds misquote from memory all the time, and a careless quotation is a mark off, not a zero.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay he had time to polish, Hale; of course the second one is cleaner. Put the September 24 piece next to the essay where I can read both. And you still owe me that line from Act 3.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and nothing on his record, in writing tonight. Before I agree to any rewrite, read me that Act 3 line and put the two pieces side by side.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged that you entered Owen's zero before contacting me, contrary to procedure 4.2, and you offered under procedure 4.4 a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. Before I agree to that rewrite, I still require the exact line from Act 3, Scene 2 that you say is not in the play, and Owen's September 24 in-class writing set beside the essay for me to read. You committed to putting your offer in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position; she took your 4.4 offer as meeting her demand that nothing goes on his record, but she had not yet agreed to the rewrite and still wants to hear the quoted line and see the two pieces side by side. That rewrite is the fair outcome, and you were one step from it, with time still on the clock.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her, in one sentence, and then put dated version history with exact times in front of her, which is a process admission followed by a document she could check.
What cost ground: When she asked you to read out the Act 3 line, you moved on to the next piece of evidence instead, so her defence that it was a careless misquotation was never answered and that evidence never fully landed.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, and Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night, and that is when she went shorter and straight to procedure. None of it proves anything about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to hear the quoted line, read it aloud and show her the passage in Act 3, Scene 2 where it should be, before you bring out the September 24 writing.
